title: Pressure Thermostat: per-entity circuit thermostat with probabilistic backoff and quarantine-based fallback routing
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Problem statement:

We need a more predictable, tenant-aware mechanism for tripping and recovering model/dependency circuits under load spikes and degradation that (1) limits noisy oscillation when endpoints recover, (2) chooses safe fallback routes deterministically, and (3) gives SREs knobs to tune aggressiveness by workload. Current threshold-based breakers cause frequent flapping for bursty workloads and don’t account for tenant priority or model affinity.

Proposal (high level):
Implement a circuit 'thermostat' abstraction per dependency/model/tenant. The thermostat computes a continuous pressure score (0..1) using: latency/ERROR rate quantiles, in-flight queue depth, and short-term token throughput. Trip occurs when pressure crosses a configurable high-water mark with a hysteresis window; recovery uses a staged cooling schedule (probabilistic backoff + shadow probes) rather than an immediate open-after-Xs approach. When tripped, traffic is routed to a quarantined fallback pool ordered by safety score (latency, cost, semantic fidelity). A probabilistic backoff factor gradually permits a controlled percentage of requests through to the primary to revalidate recovery.

Key behaviors to implement: 
- Per-entity scoring: tenant/model/dependency keys contribute to pressure with tunable weights.
- Hysteresis smoothing: exponential moving average + spike dampener to prevent flapping.
- Probabilistic rejoin: after trip, allow p(t) percent of requests to pass where p(t) increases by schedule until stability observed.
- Quarantine routing: choose fallback candidate(s) from an ordered list; time-boxed quarantine with automatic re-evaluation.
- Shadow calibration: mirror a small fraction of traffic to candidate fallbacks for offline quality scoring and to calibrate safety_score.

Acceptance criteria:
- New thermostat runs in serving runtime and exposes metrics for pressure, trip_state, quarantine_candidates, rejoin_probability, and last_probe_result.
- End-to-end tests: deterministic trip/recovery in synthetic load harness, and canary rollout passes with no >2x SLA violations during transition.
- Dashboard: Grafana panels for per-tenant pressure distributions, trip counts, and rollback probes.
- Rollout plan with staged canary and kill-switch.

Implementation notes / design decisions so far:
- We will treat pressure as a linear combination: 0.5*latency_q95_norm + 0.3*error_rate_norm + 0.2*inflight_norm, with config overrides per tenant. (Config defaults tuned from historical traces.)
- Use EMA with alpha=0.15 for smoothing; add a spike detector: if instantaneous pressure > 3x short-term median, apply a transient multiplier to avoid immediate trips (prevents trips on extremely short bursts).
- Probabilistic rejoin uses a beta schedule: p(t) = min(1, base + k*attempts) where base defaults to 0.05 and k=0.15. First probe routes single request per minute; if success metrics stable for 30s window, increase p(t).
- Quarantine candidates are chosen from model variants & regional replicas ordered by safety_score = 0.6*latency_rank + 0.3*semantic_score + 0.1*cost_rank. Semantic_score obtained from offline eval harness + shadowed request scoring pipeline.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Emit pressure gauge (time series per key), trip events (with reason tags), probe results, quarantine transitions.
- Create alert when rolling trip rate > threshold (configurable default 1% of requests/min) and when mean recovery time > expected_cooldown*2.
- Link to SLO dashboard: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/serving/thermostat-slo (placeholder)

Rollout plan:
1) Unit + integration tests in emulator + runtime feature flag.
2) Shadow run in region-1 for low-risk customers (mirror traffic) for 48h to calibrate safety_score.
3) Canary enable for 5% of traffic on internal tenants (Cycle 41).
4) Gradually increase canary to 25% and then 100% across non-enterprise tenants over 2 weeks with a manual pause at each step.
5) Enterprise/Dedicated tenants opt-in with conservative defaults.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Weighting scheme per tenant: should weights be editable via Console or only via infra config? (PM prefers Console; infra prefers config for auditability.)
- How aggressive should the probabilistic backoff be for high-priority tenants vs free tier?
- Whether to allow cross-model fallback (use cheaper model) vs same-model degraded mode—both supported but default policy will prefer same-architecture variants.

Related artifacts:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INFR/Pressure+Thermostat+Design
- Synthetic load harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1187
- Shadow scoring pipeline PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/412
- Incident that motivated this: https://incidents.redwood.example/2024-11-03-surge-model-failure-postmortem

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- ENG: implement runtime thermostat scorer + metric emission (owner: Marco) — PR draft created.
- SRE: add Grafana panels and create alertbook entries (owner: Jordan Kim).
- PM: finalize Console config UX for per-tenant knobs (owner: Lina Gomez).
- Design: produce compact UIs for quarantine override flow.

Blockers:
- Need safety_score data from offline evals pipeline (PR 412 above) — blocking final quarantine selection logic.
- Security needs to sign off on mirrored traffic policy for shadowing (ticket pending).
updates: 2025-01-15: Spike finished—prototype thermostat scorer implemented and validated locally against synthetic traces. Observed 40% reduction in flapping compared to threshold-only baseline.

2025-01-22: Design review with PM and SRE; agreed to start with Console-exposed conservative knobs (max_pressure, cooldown_base, rejoin_base) and keep advanced weights in infra config for auditability.
2025-01-28: PR created for runtime changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1187. Needs integration tests and performance bench.
2025-02-02: Safety engineering requested clarification on shadow traffic retention—opened issue SECURITY-204. Waiting for security review before shadow run in prod region.
acceptance_criteria: Thermostat scorer deployed behind feature flag in runtime and emits required metrics.
Automated tests validate trip and staged rejoin behavior deterministically.
Shadow calibration produces safety_score for at least top-10 fallback candidates per model within 48h.
Canary unlock runs without causing >2x observed SLO violations for canary customers.
Runbook updated with rollback steps and emergency kill-switch (route_all_to_primary=false).
rollout_plan: increase 25% non-enterprise (1 week) — audit and adjust weights
wider rollout with enterprise opt-in and Console defaults
risks: Shadowing may expose PII if not redacted—work with Security to ensure payload sanitization.
Incorrect safety_score can send traffic to semantically worse fallbacks; we mitigate via conservative defaults and human-in-the-loop overrides.
Complexity in per-tenant configs may increase operational burden—provide sane defaults and strong visibility.
notes: This approach intentionally favors conservative recovery to avoid oscillation seen in 2024-11 incident.
If the probabilistic rejoin shows slow convergence in prod, we will add adaptive learning to tune k and base automatically based on observed probe outcomes.
Consider follow-up work: expose per-tenant cost-vs-quality tradeoff slider in Console.
